newsitem.title: JAPAN: CYCLING - BELGIAN MUSEEUW TAKES WORLD CUP.
newsitem.headline: CYCLING - BELGIAN MUSEEUW TAKES WORLD CUP.

text.p: Belgian Johan Museeuw clinched his second successive World Cup title on Sunday when his nearest rival failed to win the Japan Cup cycle road race.
Museeuw's victory was automatically confirmed when his Italian rival for the World Cup title, Andrea Ferrigato failed to win the 11th and last round of the World Cup.
Musseuw, winner of the world road race title in Lugano, Switzerland, two weeks ago on his 31st birthday, finished 26th in the 179.5-km race. Ferrigato finished 25th.

Before Sunday's race Musseuw had 162 World Cup points, 36 points ahead of Ferrigato and 38 clear of another Italian Michele Bartoli. Fifty points awaited the winner of the 179.5-km race in northern Japan.
Bartoli did not contest the deciding race.
Museeuw won only one World Cup race this year, the prestigious Paris-Roubaix in April, but he has 65 race victories since turning professional in 1988.
"I feel tired after racing up to this time of the season... But I am not thinking of retiring," an exhausted Museeuw said after clinching his second World Cup title.
Earlier this month, Museeuw threatened to retire after the Paris-Tours race and said he would not race in Japan because the mountainous course was too hard.
"It's not easy to win as strategically planned," he said.
"I want to eat Japanese food this evening. That's what I could not have before the race."
Mauro Gianetti of Switzerland won the Japan Cup after breaking away from the pack of six rival riders at the last eight-kilometre mark.
Pascal Herve of France finished second and Italy's Andrea Peron was third.
Sunday's race involved 12 circuits of 14.10 km and a final one of 10.30 km.

"I felt confident in winning the Japan Cup when I cleared the top of the hill in the last round," Gianetti said, referring to a steep 200-metre climb just one kilometre after the start of the last lap.
It was the first and last time a World Cup race will be held in Japan as the 11th race of the series, traditionally staged in Asia, will be scrapped from next year.
